name: sys1
commitSubject: feat: TypeLLM provider — one call answers every head (probed live)
upstreamAuthor: adelvillar1 (same author as the fork; Apache-2.0)
syncRule: upstream repos stay the development home; re-vendor by copying src/ and service/mcp_server.py at a recorded sha

fleetVendor.source: ~/Projects/sys1 branch feature/plan-surface at a landed commit
fleetVendor.note: Re-vendored from the branch's own commits (KI-029 closed): src/ and service/mcp_server.py are byte-exact to f0faebc EXCEPT src/sys1/perception.py, which is fleet's carry — the documents session's parse_document lives only in the upstream working tree (never landed on feature/plan-surface), so the copy keeps fleet HEAD's file; rsync ran without --delete for exactly this reason. The same carried-file pattern KI-003 named, on a new file, until the module lands upstream.

fleetAdditions.what: the `tool_route` task — one choice head id `capability` over the nine-class closed set plus `none`, the deferred-tool search's judgment
fleetAdditions.why: fleet's tool_search calls sys1_classify with task tool_route; the label set is the ranker's own class vocabulary (src/tool_router.rs class_terms), so the class the lane names is always one the ranker can act on

fleetAdditions.what: the `curate` task — three heads over one call: needs_recall (yes/no), focus (the corpus's 7 structure + 6 failure shapes + none), staleness (fresh/stale) — the memory curator's judgment
fleetAdditions.why: fleet's mid-run memory curation composes this verdict with its cosine drift floor; the text contract is a two-part pair (last-curated instruction + new steer) because the judgment is of the move, not one text

fleetAdditions.what: the extraction verb — the entity pass over a text through the configured vendor (entity schema, threshold, offsets + confidence), returning spans, per-field declines and named problems; plus `_log_extract`'s own `op: "extract"` JSONL line
fleetAdditions.why: the owner's 2026-11-05 ruling: sys1 abstracts the System One providers, so Fleet's extraction leg may not post to a vendor itself. LOCATE and its vendor/key now live behind this verb; the leg keeps its floors, segmentation and absence semantics in Rust
the extraction vendor is configured where the other vendors are; `_settings` reads exactly these entries, so a deployment configures the extraction vendor once

fleetAdditions.what: the `sys1_extract` tool (text + fields) and an optional `task_spec` on `sys1_classify` (the HTTP face's `task_from_spec` seam), with `task_for_arguments` pulled out so the seam is testable without a stdio session
fleetAdditions.why: the leg calls LOCATE through `sys1_extract` and VERIFY through `sys1_classify` with a per-field inline task — a caller's dynamic heads must ride the same routing and cascade a registered task gets

fleetAdditions.what: the lane's own tests (stdlib unittest): the span parse and its wrong-offset drop, the per-field decline, the no-key/parse/empty failures, the extract log line, the `extract_*` settings, the `task_spec` seam, and a stdio drive of the handler's refusals
fleetAdditions.why: the vendored tree excludes upstream tests; these are Fleet's own pins for the additions above — run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` from services/sys1

fleetAdditions.what: the `validate` task — one choice head id `validity` over supported/contradicted/unverifiable, the dream pass's evidence judgment
fleetAdditions.why: fleet's dream pass (fleet memories --validate, the memory-dreaming plan's C3) calls sys1_classify with task validate over a fact-and-transcript pair; the lane judges the fact against the evidence its `source` names, and the verdict's confidence gates the pass's acting
